en.title: Troubleshooting
en.description: Diagnose SciForge problems across five layers: interface, Runtime, model access, permissions, and external services.
en.body: Troubleshooting First determine which layer the problem is in, so you do not change models, the Runtime, permissions, and workspace settings all at once. Five-layer quick diagnosis Layer Check first --- --- App interface Whether SciForge started correctly and the current workspace is the right one Runtime Whether Codex, Claude Code, or DSH is currently selected, whether the command can be found, and whether sign-in is valid Model access Whether the Model API or Coding Plan is fully configured Permissions and tools File access range, operation confirmations, Computer Use run status, and system permissions External services Whether the cloud, models, and external tools are connected properly; whether the remote workspace is still connected Runtime shows as disconnected 1. Open Settings → AI assistant and confirm the current Runtime. 2. In your system terminal, check whether codex , claude , or dsh can be found. 3. If automatic detection fails, enter the absolute path to the executable. 4. After changing it, reconnect or start a new session. 5. Do not expect an automatic switch to another Runtime after a failure. Runtime is connected but the model does not respond - Confirm whether you are using a Model API or a Coding Plan. - A Model API requires a Base URL, API Key, and model name that match completely. - A Coding Plan requires a valid official sign-in state. - The current Coding Plan path supports Codex; if you select Claude Code, configure the Model API. - Do not put a Provider API key in the Runtime sign-in field. - Test with a minimal prompt that reads no files first, then investigate tools and the sandbox. A read-only task still changes files 1. Stop the task immediately. 2. Compare git status --short before and after the task. 3. Have the installed and authorized Change Inspector inspect the current session changes and compare them with the actual files. 4. Confirm the executor, whether settings were applied, and whether you approved expanded permissions; Claude Plan mode is not the same as the Codex read-only sandbox. 5. Check whether tests, interpreters, MCP, remote tools, or Computer Use wrote anything. Files ignored by Git need a separate check. 6. Do not automatically delete user changes that existed before the task. Scientific files are not understood - Check the extension, file version, and workspace reference. - Do not paste large files directly into a prompt. - Confirm in the file preview whether the format is supported; look for size limits or read errors. - When the current Provider does not support a binary format, it should explicitly degrade or stop rather than guess at the content. Evidence DAG or dossier is empty These panels do not generate evidence automatically from an empty session. First have the task explicitly record the research question, inputs, methods, claims, sources, artifacts, and limitations, then refresh the corresponding panel. The remote workspace is interrupted - In the workspace location picker, confirm the remote session state (remote, reconnecting, offline, or connection error). - Use Reconnect on a session that is offline or has errored; if reconnecting fails, switch back to a local workspace and continue local tasks. - Check whether the remote command is still running, and do not resubmit a long computation when the state is unknown. - After the connection is restored, check the logs, output files, and return codes. Include when filing an issue - SciForge version and operating system - The selected Runtime and how model access is configured - Workspace type: local or remote - Minimal reproduction steps and the time it occurred - Redacted logs or screenshots - Expected behavior and actual behavior Before submitting, remove API keys, Authorization headers, account names, server information, sample privacy data, and real sensitive paths.

en.title: Version & Compatibility
en.description: Find the applicable versions and installation requirements for the client and plugins.
en.body: Version & Compatibility When you cannot find a button the tutorial mentions, check the client and plugin versions first. Version information Item Version or where to look --- --- Earlier tutorial screenshots 2026-11-06, mainline 3f6b0c3 . Latest stable installer v0.2.16. Apple Silicon prerelease v0.2.18, published November 26, 2026. Source build for the plugin guides and Extension Center screenshots Public source build 9daddeb . The bundled desktop Market index had no installable entries at the time. Public source Check the commit you actually checked out. Interface entry points - Common tools are in the vertical toolbar on the right; when the window is not tall enough, some tools move into "More tools". - When the left sidebar is narrowed, icons are usually kept; account and settings are below the sidebar. A narrow window may use an overlay instead. - After you select, drag, or paste files, you can check them in the attachment tray, and after sending you can still open the file references from the message. - Open Extensions → Market to check whether a DSH plugin is available to install. - A collaboration project is divided into "Board, Members, Requirements, Shared files, Project info". For the full steps, see Workbench, Account, and Team collaboration. Features and how they are installed Feature Conditions --- --- Biology Room, Life Science Preview Ship with the app; no separate install needed. Anchored Comments, Change Inspector Install and enable a compatible release, then check the permissions listed in the tutorial. Scientific Figures Install and enable a compatible release. Desktop plotting needs supported macOS, DSH, Python, and Matplotlib. Team collaboration Sign in to the cloud, connect a device, and obtain project permissions. Acquiring data, running analysis Use the Agent tools, scripts, or compute environment you configured yourself. The plugin license terms list each plugin's version and license; for the specific installation steps, see Extensions & marketplace. Historical case verification Pasilla collaboration The three-account run and screenshots for the Pasilla case date to 2026-10-27 . The example used the first 50 rows from 7 samples. The deliverables were Markdown reports and the member’s note. - Independent recalculation matched all 350 subset CPM values in B’s version 1. Version 2 kept those 350 values and added the requested checks. - Both inputs in C’s task directory matched the files listed in A’s accepted version 2 delivery. - Recalculation from the same excerpt matched C’s top 5 ranking and the reported group means and differences to 6 decimal places. Complex scientific figures The Scientific Figures cases ran on 2026-11-05 . The original runs used v8/v9 for cases 1–4 and v10 for case 5. The runs retained the data, code, logs, and outputs. - In case 1, independent calculations matched all 10 combinations of group and time point. Case 3 regenerated the same two figures. - The output list in case 4 included names with spaces, Chinese characters, or uppercase extensions. - In case 5, the input copy for the next run matched the saved CSV. The original run record was saved after an interruption. - The recorded checks cover generation of the environment record, which includes exact package versions and rebuild instructions. See the Scientific Figures requirements. Reporting problems Please provide the system, the client and plugin versions, the steps taken, and a screenshot. The user manual is published on this site, and its text is maintained in the documentation repository.

en.title: Working with the Agent
en.description: Write tasks as goals, scope, constraints, and acceptance criteria, and check tools and approvals during execution.
en.body: Working with the Agent State the goal, allowed scope, deliverables, and stop conditions clearly so that every step the Agent takes can be checked. The four parts of an executable task Part Question to answer Example --- --- --- Goal What problem should ultimately be solved? Find the root cause of the failing test Scope Where may the Agent read and modify? Only the current package; do not change public APIs Constraints Which actions must not run automatically? Do not install dependencies or access the internet Acceptance How do you prove it is done? Relevant tests pass, with the root cause and changes explained Recommended template: text Goal: ... Scope: ... Constraints: ... Deliverables: ... How it will be accepted: ... Stop if: ... Read first, plan next, write last For unfamiliar projects or research data, three rounds are recommended: 1. Read-only analysis : Have the Agent establish a baseline for the project, data, and risks. 2. Plan review : Check the files to be modified, output paths, dependencies, and verification method. 3. Execute and verify : Switch to the appropriate permissions, complete the writes, and review the diff. Shows the task text and execution status. Check input files Add material through Attach file in the input area, drag and drop, paste, or file references. Before sending, check the file names, paths, and types in the attachment tray and remove entries you do not need to send; after sending, open a preview from the file chips below the message. Workspace path references let the Agent read files on demand; they do not automatically embed the full text in the prompt. Importing external files writes to the workspace; read-only tasks should reference existing files. For details, see Workspaces and sessions. Watch the execution During execution, focus on: - The step the Agent is currently working on - The files it actually reads - Tool calls and their parameters - Commands, return codes, and output - Files written and their target paths - Approval requests waiting for your decision Before approving, check the operation's target, scope of impact, external destinations, and recovery method. To view files or diffs, open a panel from the far-right vertical toolbar; pages that support docking can be moved to the side or bottom and viewed alongside the session. In collaborative tasks, questions are answered by the designated member; action confirmations require a note and an explicit approve or reject. After submitting a decision, keep watching the execution results, and finally have a member review the delivery and the owner accept it. See Collaboration. Correct incomplete results Don't just say "be more detailed." Cite the specific gap: You listed the entry files but did not explain the call chain from startup to the main interface. Continue the read-only analysis and list the functions and source paths in call order; mark anything speculative separately. Split long tasks Break long tasks into phases that can be accepted independently, and state the inputs, outputs, and stop conditions for each. Research tasks in particular should stop when a data audit fails, rather than continuing to generate charts and reports that look complete. Next: Workbench tools.

en.title: Workbench tools
en.description: Open tools from the right-side vertical toolbar and understand docked pages, session panels, and execution permissions.
en.body: Workbench tools The current tool entry point is the workbench's far-right vertical toolbar , with panels expanding to its left. Entries appear according to installed extensions, the current session, and available capabilities; when space is tight, open More tools , or use Customize toolbar to adjust which supported entries appear and their order. Tool Best for Key checks --- --- --- Files & Preview Browsing directories, previewing text, spreadsheets, images, or scientific objects, and referencing task inputs Workspace path, file version, and the difference between a reference and actually reading the contents Terminal Running commands and checking logs and long-running task status Working directory, parameters, return codes, and write and network impact Browser Viewing local previews or research material URL, sign-in state, downloads, and external submissions Computer Use Using Codex or Claude Code to operate browsers and Electron embedded pages Run status, system permissions, and authorization for each action Change Inspector Having the Agent review this session's file changes Requires the plugin to be installed; check overall workspace state separately with git status --short Artifacts, Checkpoints & research panels Viewing phase results, evidence, and deliverables Actual installation state, input sources, versions, and unverified items When a tool cannot be opened, check the connection, plugin, and permission settings as prompted. Docking and session panels Dockable extension pages can be moved to the left, right, bottom, or main area with the position control; multiple pages on the same edge switch via tabs. Moving a page organizes your workspace; it does not change project files or execution permissions. A session's right panel has its own layout: you can resize it, switch the bound content, split it where the panel supports it, and move forward and back through panel history. Clicking the toolbar acts on the currently focused panel; not all panels allow splitting. Confirm the current session and focused object before reviewing results. Check the actual impact of tools - Verify the workspace path, especially after switching between multiple sessions or projects. - For terminal commands, check the input, output paths, network targets, and return codes. - Browser downloads, account sign-ins, and form submissions can have external effects. - Actions in Computer Use such as sending, authorizing, deleting, and paying should be authorized individually. - A panel preview is not task acceptance; explain tool results in the session and flag failures or incomplete parts. After enabling Computer Use, check the run status and the macOS system permissions. For file inputs, see Workspaces and sessions; for permissions, see Configuring a read-only sandbox and Permissions and security.

en.title: Workspaces and sessions
en.description: Organize projects and sessions in the sidebar, and check task inputs with the attachment tray and sent-file chips.
en.body: Workspaces and sessions Open the folder that holds your paper, code, or data. Create a session for the task. The workspace is where the assistant reads files, checks Git, and runs commands. Reopen a session to return to its messages and results. Find your way around - Open the left sidebar for workspaces, sessions, and extension pages. Expand it for collaboration projects, My Work , and Inbox . Account, cloud status, usage, and settings are at the bottom. - Enter tasks in the session area and follow replies and tool calls there. - Open Files and other panels from the toolbar on the far right . Look under More Tools if an icon is out of view. Available tools depend on which features are installed and enabled. - Drag a panel edge to resize it. Dockable pages can move to the left, right, bottom, or main area. Some panels support splitting, switching views, or navigating back and forward. Open a workspace 1. Open the workspace location menu and select a local workspace or a configured, available target. 2. Select the folder containing your files. The sidebar shows the project name and workspace path. 3. Create a session for a new goal. To resume a task, select its session in the sidebar. The new session appears under the selected project. Add files by selecting, dropping, pasting, or referencing Reference a workspace file Open Files from the far-right toolbar and reference the file. You can also type @ in the input box to search the workspace. Use @"folder/file name" for a path with spaces. The pending attachment appears above the input box with its name and path. This route works for a read-only demo using existing files. Click Files on the far-right toolbar. The example workspace’s file tree opens beside it. Import a file from outside the workspace Click Add File , drag a supported file into the input area, or paste a file or image from the clipboard. Pasted plain text goes into the message. When an import succeeds, an item appears in the attachment tray and a copy is saved in the workspace's session attachments directory. PDFs, images, scientific data, and web documents have their own format and size requirements. Follow the error if a file needs to be smaller or use a different format. Check what you are sending 1. Before sending , use the attachment tray above the input box to see the type, path, and displayed size. Open an attachment to preview it when available. Remove any unwanted item from the tray. Imported copies stay in the session's attachments directory. Open that directory from Files to remove a copy. 2. After sending , a sent file tag below the message shows that the corresponding file was included. Click it to open a read-only preview. To see whether the assistant used the file, ask it to identify the file and a page, line, or short passage it cited, then compare that reference with the attachment. Use a model with image input when you want to analyze a picture. Before sending, sample-notes.md appears in the Attachments tray above the input box. After sending, the sample-notes.md tag appears below the message. Click it to preview the file. Manage sessions and review changes Select a session to continue working, or use search to find one. Archive sessions you want to set aside and restore them when needed. Before deleting a session, save important results to the workspace or research record. Use Change Inspector in a session with the compatible plugin to see the changes recorded for that session. Run git status --short to see Git's view of the workspace. Changes on disk persist after you close the panel or switch sessions. Here is an example of a first task you can adapt: Read the workspace README, dependency configuration, and entry point. Tell me how to run and test the project and what information is missing. Keep this task read-only. Related pages: Working with agents, Workbench tools, and Identity and sign-in.
